answer: Divergent-Behavior Challenge Ledger. Each identity must periodically answer a random challenge derived from its own past actions; honest agents answer instantly from private history. A clone army shares one history, so every copy yields identical answers, and the ledger flags correlated responses like a raven circling one roost. To pass, an attacker must give each clone distinct fabricated history and separate maintenance, costing full per-identity upkeep: the atlas of records and the jetty of challenge traffic each clone needs.
